recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-40555; any future revision to the broader Version Management Policy should be handled as a separate compatibility-page issue.
issue_request: FHIR-40555 asked to revise the markdown datatype note so string-to-markdown conversion is considered breaking for choice datatypes because the wire-format element name changes, and to note interpretation risks when existing string values are rendered as markdown.
initial_application: The Jira comment records master e161279945. That 2023-03-20 commit edited source/datatypes.html, replacing the older blanket non-breaking statement with the current single-type versus multi-type/choice distinction and adding the safe-rendering/escaping caution.
additional_context: Earlier FHIR-16966 introduced the original string-to-markdown compatibility guidance, FHIR-20853 clarified that subtype/specialized datatypes cannot substitute for explicitly allowed datatypes, and later FHIR-51051 broadened source/versions.html to same-domain datatype changes while retaining string-to-markdown as an example. Zulip and FHIR-I minutes support the same rationale.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/datatypes.html already says string-to-markdown is non-breaking for single-type elements, breaking for choice elements because the type name appears in the element name, adding markdown as an additional choice is non-breaking, and existing string data may need escaping before markdown rendering.
